desk_read: Yesterday's desk flow was defined by broad short covering across equities and commodities alongside heavy long liquidation in petroleum. Nasdaq 100 saw positioning thin out by -20.2k contracts as prices rallied +3.43% on volume running at 1.1x its 20-day average. S&P 500 experienced a similar dynamic with total open interest dropping -44.1k contracts alongside a +2.33% price gain. Meanwhile, WTI Crude Oil suffered a -4.38% price drop accompanied by net long liquidation as total open interest fell -11.4k contracts, while Brent dropped -5.85% with a -1.5k contract reduction in total open interest. In contrast, Gold bucked the liquidation trend, adding +4.1k contracts in total open interest alongside a +0.97% price gain on volume at 1.2x its 20-day average.
oil_read: Yesterday's session saw steep losses, with WTI dropping -4.38% alongside a total open interest reduction of -11.4k contracts (-0.9%) and volume at 1.0x its 20-day average, signaling long liquidation. Brent (NYMEX) slumped -5.85% with total open interest down -1.5k contracts (-1.2%) and volume matching 1.0x its 20-day average, also reflecting long liquidation. Both markets maintained backwardation across their forward curves.
bias_read: WTI Crude Oil and Brent (NYMEX) both hold a neutral bias driven by long liquidation and weakening curves in backwardation, which warns of trend exhaustion as exiting positions reduce durability. Gold shows a mildly bullish bias from new longs, meaning fresh positions support the upward move. Copper posts a mildly bullish bias from short covering alongside volume 1.7x the 20-day average, where high conviction supports the current trend. Overall, widespread neutral biases from short-covering and liquidation suggest most moves lack durable backing, signaling a fragile environment across desks.
